record.original_question: Does there exist an integer d >= 3 such that for every polygon the full billiard complexity has a cubic lower bound and also an upper bound by a polynomial of degree d?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. There is d >= 3 such that the full billiard complexity for any polygon has a cubic lower bound and a degree d upper bound.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (a connected planar region bounded by finitely many straight segments). The billiard flow on $P$ is the geodesic flow of a point particle moving with unit speed inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at each side; trajectories meeting a vertex are undefined. Label the sides of $P$ by symbols from a finite alphabet $\mathcal{A}$. To each (one-sided or two-sided) billiard trajectory associate the infinite word over $\mathcal{A}$ recording the labels of the sides hit in order. The full billiard complexity $f_P(n)$ is defined as the number of distinct words of length $n$ that occur as factors of any such trajectory in $P$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $d\ge 3$ such that, for every polygon $P$, there are constants $c_1=c_1(P)>0$, $c_2=c_2(P)>0$ and an integer $n_0=n_0(P)$ with
$$c_1\, n^3 \;\le\; f_P(n)\;\le\; c_2\, n^d \qquad\text{for all } n\ge n_0\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes cubic complexity growth for typical/rational polygons and obtains polynomial lower bounds for special families (e.g., almost every right triangle), but a uniform polynomial upper bound of fixed degree d valid for every polygon, together with a cubic lower bound for every polygon, has not been proved. The conjecture appears to remain open, with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of polygonal billiards (arXiv:2312.04133)
status_evidence.snippet: Show that the complexity of the billiard in a typical polygon grows cubically; establish an upper bound on the upper metric complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Provides cubic growth for typical polygons and polynomial upper bounds, but does not establish a uniform polynomial-degree upper bound for all polygons.

status_evidence.title: Complexity and growth for polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Cubic upper and lower bounds in the rational case.
status_evidence.claim: Cubic bounds known for rational polygons; general polygon case remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Complexity for billiards in regular N-gons (arXiv:2502.17627)
status_evidence.claim: Specific polygon classes analyzed; full conjecture for arbitrary polygons not settled.
